title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing + padding-minimization heuristics (v2)
author: Amira Patel
description: Motivation: serving workloads show high wasted compute due to padding in continuous batching when sequence length variance is high. This PR implements a second-generation sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristic that reduces token-level padding while preserving batching opportunities and latency SLOs. Summary: 1) introduce an adaptive bucketer that picks bucket boundaries from observed request length distribution with a penalty term for creating too many buckets; 2) add a fast padding-minimization pass that opportunistically pads shorter requests within a batch only to the next bucket boundary; 3) wire the heuristic into the continuous batching scheduler and the KV-cache-aware planner so that cache hit locality is preserved when merging batches; 4) expose tunables (max_buckets, merge_penalty, bucket_min_size) and telemetry to the console. Implementation details: - Bucketer computes histogram of recent sequence lengths (sliding window) and runs a greedy boundary selection that optimizes (padded_tokens + alpha * buckets) where alpha is merge_penalty. - We maintain per-model, per-shard exemplar histograms to avoid global coordination; this keeps decision latency < 200us. - Scheduler changes: when forming a batch the scheduler consults bucket assignment to prefer grouping same-bucket requests; if time-since-first-request exceeds batch_wait_ms threshold, it will apply padding-minimization to avoid starvation. - KV cache integration: added a compatibility check to only allow cross-bucket merging when all requests share compatible cache key prefixes (same conversation/stream id or empty). This prevents cache fragmentation. - Safety and rollout: default parameters are conservative (max_buckets=8, alpha=0.02) and the feature is gated behind a feature-flag per-deployment. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on p4d.24xlarge with Llama-2-13B quantized path show ~12% throughput improvement and ~8% reduction in mean padded tokens for high-variance input traces (chat+search mix). End-to-end latency p95 remained within SLO (+1.5ms). Memory overhead: +1.8% peak GPU memory due to histogram bookkeeping. Backwards compatibility: if feature-flag off, scheduler reverts to previous continuous-batching behavior. Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary customers for two weeks, enable on Dedicated pools with opt-in for Private installs. See release_notes for user-facing notes.

discussion: Q: How do we avoid creating too many tiny buckets? A: greedy selector includes penalty term (alpha) to penalize bucket count; default alpha set to 0.02 after grid search.

Q: Will this hurt KV cache hit rates? A: We only allow cross-bucket merging when cache key prefixes are compatible; added metric to monitor hit-rate delta. Observed <1% hit-rate regression in our traces.
Rollout note: Feature gated; enabled in canary and dedicated pools first. Recommend 2-week observation before wider rollout.
release_notes: runtime: improved dynamic batching by sequence length — reduces padded tokens and improves throughput for high-variance workloads. Feature is behind a feature-flag and safe by default.
